question.text: The conflict spread when Germany attacked this neutral country hoping to capture Liege ("leezh") and outflank the French. Instead, Britain entered the war on the Allied side.
question.clue: One-third of the votes cast in an election in this country set up by the provisional government of Charles Rogier were left blank in protest.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Netherlands, whose name literally means "low-lying countries"
swap.text: Part of the modern-day Netherlands gained independence from the Spanish Empire in a war named for this many years, which is how long it lasted.

question.text: British journalist Charles Mackay's book Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds documented the 1637 economic bubble caused by a sharp decline in the price of tulips in this European country with capital Amsterdam.
question.clue: This European country traded at Dejima under the policy of sakoku , which made it the only Western nation to trade with Japan for over two hundred years.

swap.text: The Dutch revolt against Spanish rule is generally known as this war, referring to its length. It was ended by the Peace of Munster and the independence of the Dutch Republic.
swap.clue: The first assassination of a head of state by handgun was carried out by Balthasar Gerard during this war.

question.leadin: Name the following about the European origins of the Black Legend.
question.text: This port city was subject to the 1576 "Spanish Fury" by unpaid mutinying soldiers. The collective response by the United Provinces to its destruction intensified the Eighty Years War.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.text: This Flemish geographer created a 1569 world map that represented sailing courses as straight lines and distorted Greenland to the size of Africa.
swap.clue: This University of Leuven scholar, who created a 1569 world map, led the "golden age of Netherlandish cartography." This engraver, who coined the term "atlas," names a widely-used but controversial map "projection."

question.leadin: In September of 1944, over 40,000 allied paratroopers were dropped near Arnhem in the Netherlands in an ambitious plan to end World War 2 by Christmas.
question.text: Name this failed operation. Its success depended on the taking and holding of several bridges.
question.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Belgian prime minister Gaston Eyskens (AY-skens).
swap.text: Eyskens hailed from this Dutch-speaking region in Belgium's north, which he governed alongside the French-speaking Wallonia.
swap.clue: A shibboleth was used here prior to the Battle of the Golden Spurs, and parts of the "race to the sea" occurred here, ending after the opening of the sea-locks during the Battle of the Yser.

question.leadin: This man became one of the first heads of state to die by handgun when Balthasar Gerard assassinated him in 1584.
question.text: Name this stadtholder who gave a speech on religious toleration in the Spanish Council of State and urged the Sea Beggars to petition Margaret of Parma to end religious persecution.
question.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I, Prince of Orange, Count of Nassau or Willem I or Willem de Zwijger; prompt on "William of Orange"]
question.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

swap.text: During Peter's Grand Embassy, he worked as a carpenter for this company in Saardam. This company set up a base in Jakarta in 1619.
swap.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [or Dutch East Indies Company; or United East India Company; or Vereenigde Oost-indische Compagnie]
swap.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about particularly old economic bubbles.
question.text: Tulip mania occurred in this nation in the 1630's when the speculation of Amsterdam-based traders drove the price of specific tulip bulbs incredibly high, only for the prices to suddenly crash.
question.answerHtml: Dutch Republic [or Republic of the Seven United Netherlands; prompt on “Holland”]
question.clue: The first recorded speculative bubble occurred when the price of tulips in this country grew exponentially and then collapsed in 1637.

swap.text: The Eighty Years War was sparked by a rebellion led by William the Silent, a member of this Dutch royal house.
swap.clue: A group supported by this dynasty that adopted crescent-shaped symbols for Ottoman support was the Sea Beggars.

question.leadin: Answer the following about historical periods depicted in the books of Adam Hochschild.
question.text: Hochschild's most famous book is named for this king's Ghost. This king of Belgium oversaw the Congo Free State as a personal fiefdom and directed his Force Publique to carry out forced amputations to collect rubber.
question.clue: Those lands had been gained for this man after he sent Henry Morton Stanley to negotiate with tribal chiefs.

swap.leadin: After its import from the Ottoman Empire in the 16th century, this plant became a status symbol and caused a speculative bubble in 1634.
swap.text: Name this plant whose prices skyrocketed during a namesake 17th century "mania."
swap.clue: Beginning in the Netherlands during the Dutch Golden Age, forty of these flowers sold for 100,000 guilders.

question.leadin: At the confederal level, the holder of this position in Holland received the title of Captain-General of the army and Admiral-General of the navy.
question.text: Name these governors of provinces including Friesland ("FREEZ-lont") and Utrecht. Orangists supported hereditary succession for this position, which they finally succeeded in amalgamating into a general form across all provinces in 1747.
question.answerHtml: stadtholder [or stadtholder-general; or General Stadtholder; or stadhouder; or erfstadhouder; or stadhouder-generaal]
question.clue: Reforms to pike and shot tactics made by a holder of this office directly inspired those made by Gustavus Adolphus.

swap.text: Though now only the eighth-largest city in the Netherlands, this city's historical importance is seen in its three changes of ownership during the Dutch war of independence and in Charles II's "declaration" from this city regarding the resumption of the English monarchy.
swap.clue: A declaration named for this city was issued in response to an offer from General George Monck and promised to pardon all who recognized Charles II as the British monarch.

question.text: Ludvigsen was influenced by the Provo movement, which passed urbanist "White Plans" in this non-Danish city. This city's own squatters movement was involved in its 1980 coronation riots.
question.clue: A failed 1650 attack on this city, where wealthy regents like the Bicker brothers held power, preceded a 22-year vacancy of leadership ending in the "Disaster Year."

swap.text: In 1661, Portugal signed this treaty with the Dutch government of Johan de Witt. In it, Portugal ceded its possessions in Asia to the Dutch, but kept control of possessions in the New World and Africa.

question.leadin: After the Peace of Westphalia, the newly-independent Dutch Republic was ruled by a faction of urban merchants, in particular those based in Amsterdam.
question.text: All of that ended in 1672, the Rampjaar or disaster year, when this man was deposed after twenty-five years as Grand Pensionary and then lynched after French forces advanced through the Spanish Netherlands as far as Utrecht.
question.clue: In order to focus on his country's invasion in the War of Devolution, this man quickly negotiated the Treaty of Breda to end a war with England.

swap.leadin: Since their pay had been confiscated by Elizabeth I en route to them, angry Spanish tercios decided to carry out this action as a way of compensating themselves for their lost wages.
swap.text: Name this 1576 action, sometimes called the Spanish Fury, in which forces under Sancho d'Avila pillaged a wealthy port city for three days straight. Rather than breaking the will of the revolting Dutch, this event instead strengthened their resolve.
swap.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.
